title: Finite-type invariant subalgebras and descent of module finiteness over arbitrary bases
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $R$ be a commutative finite-type $e$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let a finite group $H$ act on $R$ by $e$-algebra automorphisms. Put $A=R^H=\{r\in R:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$, as an $e$-subalgebra of $R$. Then $R$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], and $A$ is of finite type over $e$. If $R$ is reduced, meaning that $r^n=0$ for $n\ge1$ implies $r=0$, then $A$ is reduced. Moreover, for every commutative $e$-algebra $C$ and $e$-algebra map $u:C\to R$ whose image lies in $A$, if $R$ is a finitely generated $C$-module via $u$, then $A$ is a finitely generated $C$-module via the corestriction of $u$. More precisely, in this last situation the image $C'=u(C)\subseteq A$ is a finite-type Noetherian $e$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $A$ is a finite $C'$-module. Neither injectivity of $u$ nor a Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis on $C$ is assumed. No faithfulness, freeness or invertibility of $|H|$ is assumed.

Integrality is supplied by the existing finite-group invariant-ring node, and finite-submodule finiteness by the existing Noetherian module nodes.

proof.text: Because the action is by $e$-algebra automorphisms, the image of $e$ lies in $A$. Apply the integrality clause of [lem-dl-a1-finite-invariant-prime-orbits-residues] to the finite group $H$ acting on the commutative ring $R$. Thus each $r\in R$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0BRI, lemma-one-orbit, first sentence of proof.

proof.text: Choose $e$-algebra generators $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ of $R$; they also generate $R$ over $A$, since $e$ maps into $A$. For each $i$ take a monic equation of degree $d_i\geq1$ from Step 1. Replacing $r_i^{d_i}$ by the lower powers in that equation and inducting on the exponent reduces every monomial to an $A$-linear combination of $r_1^{j_1}\cdots r_n^{j_n}$ with $0\leq j_i<d_i$. These finitely many monomials therefore generate $R$ over $A$. When $n=0$ the sole monomial is $1$. This is the explicit reduction in Stacks Tag 00GM, lemma-characterize-integral.

The field $e$ is Noetherian: an ideal containing a nonzero $x$ contains $x^{-1}x=1$, so every ideal is either generated by $0$ or by $1$. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] with base $e$, ambient algebra $R$ and subalgebra $A$. The ambient algebra is of finite type by hypothesis and is module-finite over $A$ by Step 2. Hence $A$ is of finite type over $e$.

source.place: Tag 00IS, lemma-Artin-Tate, with base e and subalgebra A.

proof.text: If $R$ is reduced and $a\in A$ satisfies $a^m=0$ with $m\geq1$, its image in $R$ has the same vanishing power and is zero. The subring inclusion is injective, so $a=0$ in $A$. Thus $A$ is reduced.

source.place: Reducedness by the injective subring inclusion; direct argument from the definition in the item.

proof.text: For the additional hypothesis on $u:C\to R$, put $C\prime=u(C)\subseteq A$. It is an $e$-subalgebra because $u$ is an $e$-algebra map. If $x_1,\ldots,x_s$ generate $R$ over $C$, each expression $r=\sum_i u(c_i)x_i$ is already a $C\prime$-linear expression. Thus the same elements generate $R$ over $C\prime$, including when $R$ is the zero ring.

source.place: Image-subalgebra reduction before the second application of Tag 00IS, lemma-Artin-Tate; direct coefficient calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-artin-tate-subalgebra-finite-type] again, now with base $e$, ambient algebra $R$ and subalgebra $C\prime$. Step 3 proved that $e$ is Noetherian, $R$ is of finite type over $e$ by hypothesis, and Step 5 proves module-finiteness over $C\prime$. Hence $C\prime$ is of finite type over $e$. The ring clause of [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], applied to $C\prime$ over the field $e$, makes $C\prime$ Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00IS, lemma-Artin-Tate, applied to the image subalgebra; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: The inclusion $A\subseteq R$ is a $C\prime$-submodule, since $C\prime\subseteq A$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] using the Noetherian ring $C\prime$ from Step 6 and the finite $C\prime$-module $R$ from Step 5. This gives finite generators $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ of $A$ over $C\prime$. For each expression $a=\sum_j b_j a_j$, choose $c_j\in C$ with $u(c_j)=b_j$; then $a=\sum_j c_j\cdot a_j$ for the corestricted $C$-action. Thus the same generators make $A$ finite over $C$, as required.

source.place: Tag 00IK, lemma-Noetherian-basic, second assertion; elementary lifting of coefficients along C onto its image.
